ip_top_stories.title: GEMA Wins Copyright Case Against Suno AI in Germany
ip_top_stories.summary: A Munich Regional Court has ruled that AI music company Suno illegally trained its model on copyright-protected music without a licence, finding in favour of German performing rights society GEMA. The ruling is considered Europe's first major AI music copyright decision and bars Suno from using GEMA-protected works in its training. The case marks a significant precedent for how AI training on copyrighted material is treated under European law.

ip_top_stories.title: Reddit's DMCA Claims Against Perplexity AI and SerpApi Survive Legal Challenge
ip_top_stories.summary: A US court has allowed Reddit's DMCA claims against Perplexity AI and scraping service SerpApi to proceed, rejecting the defendants' bids to have the case dismissed under a broad reading of the DMCA. The ruling keeps alive Reddit's lawsuit over unauthorised scraping of its data for AI training purposes. The decision is a significant procedural win for platforms seeking to protect their content from AI data harvesting.

ip_top_stories.title: Midjourney Copied Thousands of Car Photos to Train AI, Suit Says
ip_top_stories.summary: A new lawsuit alleges that AI image generator Midjourney copied thousands of copyrighted car photographs without authorisation to train its AI model. The case adds to the growing body of litigation targeting AI companies over their use of copyrighted material in training datasets. No further details on the plaintiffs or jurisdiction were specified in the report.

ip_top_stories.title: Anthropic Says Authors' New AI Copyright Claims Fall Flat
ip_top_stories.summary: Anthropic has filed arguments contending that authors' recently added copyright claims in their lawsuit against the company lack legal merit. The filing pushes back against plaintiffs' attempts to expand the scope of the case. The dispute is part of a broader wave of litigation by authors against AI developers over alleged unauthorised use of books for training.

ip_top_stories.title: GCC Bans AI-Generated Code Over GPL Copyright Fears
ip_top_stories.summary: The GCC (GNU Compiler Collection) project has moved to ban code derived from large language models due to concerns that such code may carry copyright implications incompatible with the GPLv3 licence. The decision reflects growing unease within open-source communities about the legal provenance of LLM-generated contributions. The move could have significant implications for how AI tools are used in open-source software development.

ip_further_links.title: AI vs. Authors Update: Court Approves Historic Anthropic Settlement While Meta Litigation Continues
ip_further_links.summary: A court has approved a settlement in an AI copyright case against Anthropic brought by authors, while separate litigation against Meta over similar training data claims continues.

ip_further_links.title: OpenAI's EU AI Act Statement Skips Training Data: Copyright Gap Activates Sunday
ip_further_links.summary: Analysis finds that OpenAI's statement on EU AI Act compliance omits any reference to training data transparency, raising concerns about a copyright disclosure gap as new provisions come into force.

ip_further_links.title: Deep Fakes, Real Transparency: Labelling Deep Fakes and AI-Generated Public-Interest Text
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis examines emerging legal and policy frameworks requiring labelling of deepfakes and AI-generated content, particularly where such content intersects with the public interest.

ip_further_links.title: Paperback Writer, Meet the Shredder
ip_further_links.summary: A commentary piece examines the impact of AI-generated content on the book publishing industry and the challenges facing human authors.

ip_further_links.title: Never Too Late: If you missed the IPKat last week!
ip_further_links.summary: IPKat's weekly roundup covers recent developments in intellectual property law including AI copyright cases and related legal commentary.
